Here is the analysis and the ranked list. The Plex database copy I made on docker-host has been removed.

## What your listening history says

I read the Plex library database directly on docker-host and used your account's track plays as the main signal, since you only have 9 five-star ratings. The picture is consistent across about 10,000 plays.

- **Sample-based, soulful boom bap is the core.** Donuts is your single most-played album, well ahead of anything else. Madvillainy, Illmatic, 3 Feet High and Rising, MM..FOOD, The Renaissance and Zion VIII all sit high. You return to the same Donuts tracks repeatedly, which means the source material is doing a lot of the work.
- **Jazz-inflected, groove-led modern rap** dominates the rest: Little Simz, Oddisee, Saba with No ID, Noname, Kota the Friend, Mac Miller. These are mostly live-band or lightly sampled, so the sample trail is thinner.
- **Your jazz is jazz-funk and fusion, not bebop.** Thundercat, Kiefer, Butcher Brown, Azymuth, Roy Hargrove's RH Factor, Makaya McCraven, Ezra Collective, Bitches Brew and On the Corner. That points squarely at 1970s CTI, Blue Note and Mizell-era records.
- **Soul is present but shallow.** You own three Marvin Gaye albums and played the Yasiin Gaye mashup 59 times, and the Common x Stevie Wonder mashup 42 times. You own no Stevie Wonder, no Roy Ayers, no Donald Byrd and no Michael Jackson.

WhoSampled blocks automated access, so sample credits below come from Wikipedia liner-note sections, Tracklib's Donuts breakdown, and WhoSampled entries surfaced via search. None of the 15 albums is in your library.

## The 15 albums, most likely to land first

1. **Ahmad Jamal Trio, The Awakening (1970).** "I Love Music" is Nas "The World Is Yours", "Dolphin Dance" is Common "Resurrection", "Swahililand" is De La Soul "Stakes Is High". You own all three source albums. Piano trio with the same restraint you get from Kiefer and Glasper.
2. **Stevie Wonder, Songs in the Key of Life (1976).** The biggest gap in your collection. "Sir Duke" is Tribe's "Footprints", Stevie is credited on De La's "Cruel Summers", and A Common Wonder is built entirely on his catalogue.
3. **Roy Ayers Ubiquity, Everybody Loves the Sunshine (1976).** The title track is on De La's "Cruel Summers Bring FIRE LIFE!!", one of your top Cabin in the Sky plays. Vibes-led jazz-funk that sits right between Thundercat and Azymuth.
4. **Donald Byrd, Black Byrd (1973).** "Flight Time" is the backbone of both "N.Y. State of Mind" and its 2025 sequel on Light-Years. Mizell brothers production, the blueprint for the sound Butcher Brown chases. Follow with Places and Spaces.
5. **Minnie Riperton, Adventures in Paradise (1975).** "Baby, This Love I Have" is "Check the Rhime" and "Inside My Love" is "Lyrics to Go". Stevie Wonder's band plays on it.
6. **Ronnie Foster, Two Headed Freap (1972).** "Mystic Brew" is "Electric Relaxation". Blue Note organ funk, short and replayable.
7. **Eddie Kendricks, People… Hold On (1972).** "My People… Hold On" is Dilla's "People", one of your most-played Donuts tracks. "Girl You Need a Change of Mind" is one of the most sampled records in existence.
8. **Ramsey Lewis, Salongo (1976).** "Dreams" is Dilla's "Glazed". Earth, Wind & Fire era Ramsey, so it leans the same way as your Kiefer and RH Factor plays.
9. **Cortex, Troupeau Bleu (1975).** "Huit Octobre 1971" is MF DOOM's "One Beer". French jazz-funk with a Brazilian tilt, the closest thing on this list to Azymuth.
10. **Grant Green, Alive! (1970).** The live "Down Here on the Ground" is "Vibes and Stuff". Long, loose guitar funk that rewards full-album listening.
11. **Weldon Irvine, Spirit Man (1975).** "We Gettin' Down" is "Award Tour". Irvine is Q-Tip's favourite well and shows up across the Tribe and Dilla catalogue.
12. **Bob James, One (1974).** "Nautilus" is on "Clap Your Hands" and on dozens of other records you own by Ghostface, Run-DMC and Slick Rick. CTI smooth fusion.
13. **Steely Dan, Aja (1977).** "Peg" is De La's "Eye Know". The jazziest Steely Dan record. Pair with The Royal Scam, whose "Kid Charlemagne" is Kanye's "Champion", one of your top Graduation plays.
14. **Michael Jackson, Thriller (1982).** "Human Nature" is "It Ain't Hard to Tell" and "P.Y.T." is "Good Life". Outside your genres, but two of your most-played albums lean on it and you own nothing by him.
15. **David Axelrod, Song of Innocence (1968).** Axelrod's "1000 Rads" from Seriously Deep is Nas's "Pause Tapes" on Light-Years, and his work underpins DJ Shadow's Endtroducing, which you own. Song of Innocence is the better full album.

**Near misses worth a listen:** 10cc's Sheet Music for "Workinonit", Marvin Gaye and Tammi Terrell's You're All I Need for Saba's "Every Painting Has a Price", Michael White's The Land of Spirit and Light for Saba's "Stop Playing With Me", and Kool & the Gang's Music Is the Message for Dilla's "The Diff'rence".

- **Sample-based, jazz-leaning boom bap.** Donuts, Madvillainy, Illmatic, Tribe, De La Soul, Guru's Jazzmatazz, 9th Wonder, Slum Village and the DJ Premier and Pete Rock cuts on Light-Years and Cabin in the Sky.
- **Introspective, soulful modern rap.** Oddisee, Saba, Kota the Friend, Noname, Mac Miller, Little Simz, J. Cole and Mick Jenkins dominate your play counts.
- **UK rap with live jazz around it.** Little Simz is your most-played artist, with Dave, Bashy, Stormzy and Ezra Collective behind her.

## The 10 artists and their best album

1. **Gang Starr, Moment of Truth (1998).** DJ Premier produced your sixth most-played album and three tracks on Cabin in the Sky, and you own Guru's Jazzmatazz but no Gang Starr. This is the pair at their peak.
2. **Pete Rock & CL Smooth, Mecca and the Soul Brother (1992).** Pete Rock produced "The Package" and "Different World", both in your Cabin in the Sky top plays. This is the definitive jazz-loop record of the era and sits directly beside Illmatic and Low End Theory.
3. **Little Brother, The Minstrel Show (2005).** 9th Wonder produced the whole thing and you played Zion VIII 50 times. Phonte's warm, conversational writing is the direct ancestor of Oddisee and Saba, and Rapsody came up under this crew.
4. **Blu & Exile, Below the Heavens (2007).** Soul-sample production under a young rapper working out his life. If Kota the Friend, Saba and Oddisee are your comfort listens, this is the record they all cite.
5. **Loyle Carner, hugo (2022).** UK rapper with live jazz players, closer in tone to Little Simz and Dave than anyone else in your library. Slower and more domestic than Simz, which suits your Kiefer and Ezra Collective plays.
6. **Souls of Mischief, 93 'til Infinity (1993).** You own Tribe, The Pharcyde, Digable Planets and Jurassic 5 but not the Hieroglyphics side of that scene. Jazz loops, fast interplay, and the title track alone justifies it.
7. **Black Milk, Album of the Year (2010).** Detroit producer-rapper who inherited the Dilla and Slum Village lineage you already own, with eLZhi as a regular collaborator. Live drums over chopped soul.
8. **Big K.R.I.T., 4eva Is a Mighty Long Time (2017).** Southern soul rap for the OutKast, Scarface, JID and EarthGang thread. Self-produced double album, one disc for the car, one disc for late nights.
9. **Reflection Eternal, Train of Thought (2000).** Talib Kweli with Hi-Tek producing, from the same year as Black on Both Sides. You own seven Kweli albums but not this one, and most people rate it above all of them.
10. **Homeboy Sandman, Hallways (2014).** Wordy, funny, off-kilter rapper who later made two albums with Aesop Rock. Fits the Aesop, Open Mike Eagle and Quelle Chris corner of your collection, with Stones Throw production.
